Subject: Invoice 7832 — payment failed; next steps and VAT entity question

Hi Alex / GreenTide finance team,

We tried to collect payment for invoice #7832 (period May 2027) today and the attempt failed while routing through our EU acquirer. Stripe returned an "acquirer_decline" (code 54) and the transaction was not captured. The invoice is currently overdue by 3 days.

Two quick asks so we can resolve before a chargeback escalates:
- Can you confirm whether GreenTide paid this invoice directly via bank transfer? If so, please attach the remittance (reference shown on invoice: GT-INV-7832).
- If not, would you be able to update the card on file or provide an alternate payment method? We can route a one-time tokenized link if you prefer.

Also: our system flagged a VAT entity mismatch (invoice billed to Redwood EU SARL but the payment instrument appears associated with a non-EU issuing bank). If you have a different billing entity to use for VAT purposes (e.g., GreenTide EU / VAT ID), please let us know — that may affect acquirer routing.

Attachments: [attachment: invoice_7832.pdf (PDF, 92KB)]

Thanks — if it's helpful I can set up a quick call with payments ops to walk through a token-swap route.

— Aditya

Subject: Re: Fwd: Invoice 7832 — acquirer_decline + remittance attached — need ops plan

Aditya / team,

Plan below (high-level):
1) Immediate: provide GreenTide a tokenization link (PCI-compliant hosted form). If they update a card, we can attempt a one-time authorization via our secondary PSP (EU PSP B) which has a different acquirer path and higher acceptance for that issuer BIN. I can generate the link and enable a single-use token that expires in 24 hours.

2) Dispute evidence: if the bank/issuer escalates a chargeback, we should submit: invoice_7832.pdf, remittance_greentide_20270604.pdf, signed T&Cs (purchase order/SOW), API request logs showing successful provisioning of service for the May period, and the customer's account activity (IP / login + usage). I attached the internal checklist we send to Stripe for merchant disputes.

3) Timeline: Stripe typically requires an evidence submission within 7–10 calendar days after the dispute; acquirer-specific windows can be shorter. If the customer can either (a) confirm the SEPA with transaction reference or (b) update the card and allow a retry within 48 hours, we can likely avoid a formal dispute.

4) Alternate routing caveat: if we switch PSP, the customer's VAT entity needs to match the billing entity on the invoice to avoid acquirer-level tax-blocks. Alex confirmed GreenTide EU (VAT: EU123456789) — please confirm the exact invoice recipient name.

I'll open OPS ticket OPS-4572 and attach logs. Alex, can you confirm whether your treasury can provide the originating bank reference (End-to-End ID) from the SEPA instruction? That will help rebut the bank-level chargeback.

Attachments: [attachment: internal_ticket_#4572.txt (TXT, 3KB)]

— Vivek
